paragraphs: On the road back to Bianliang, refugees lined the way.
Shen Jianchen worked out the timing. Wanyan Zongwang was attacking Hebei; three months more and he would cross the Yellow River and drive straight at Bianliang.
He had to ride hard and sell every last thing he owned before the Jin army reached the city.
Shen Jianchen and Bai Feng traveled day and night. When they reached Bianliang, the Jin had not yet arrived, but the news had. The whole city was on edge, and anyone with the means was fleeing south.
The court would not let the city's high officials leave, and kept sending troops north to shore up the Yellow River line.

Back at the Prince Yi manor, Shen Jianchen told Matron Zou about Mengrong and Xilan. She grieved for a long while. When the grief had passed, she backed him all the way and told him to do what he wanted, with no holding back.
He began selling the manor and everything under his name. With the country coming apart, buyers were scarce. A month went by and nothing sold.
War had the court and its ministers too busy to care about one prince selling his property. That suited Shen Jianchen fine.
Luck arrived with Bianliang's first snow. A buyer came to the gate for the Prince Yi manor. It was Lady Wei.
Lady Wei heard he was selling to save someone, and that the someone was Youqi Jushi. She did not haggle over a single coin. She bought the manor outright.
After that, more people came for his other holdings. Ask around, and they all traced back to Lady Wei. Shen Jianchen could not thank her enough.
Once the silver was gathered, he sent Bai Feng to escort Matron Zou back to Lin'an and stay at the bamboo house for now. He himself set out for Yanjing with ten million taels in drafts.
The fighting grew tighter the farther they went. After many detours, they finally reached Yanjing.
People in Yanjing were out on the streets again, Jin folk among them. The Jin must have eased their rules and let ordinary life resume.

Shadows moved through the streets, but the bustle of wartime could not wash the bleakness out of anyone's heart. Winter cold lay over it all. Every person on the street hunched in on himself, the way the Song itself hunched in on itself, bracing against a war that would not end.
Shen Jianchen had no heart for reflection. He found Cai Jing and asked him to tell Wanyan Chi the ten million taels were ready, and urge him to release the prisoner.
Cai Jing gaped at the figure, then went to the manor and reported it to Wanyan Chi.
Wanyan Chi thought to himself: She matters that much to him? If it were me, would I trade ten million taels for one woman?
He felt the sting of that thought. Jealousy would not let him hand over the beauty. But ten million taels had walked up to his door. Free money was free money.
"Tell him to come to the manor tomorrow. Money on one side, woman on the other."

Cai Jing could not read him at all. He took it as a promise to release her and said, "Your Highness is far wiser than the Prince Yi of Song. How can a woman compare to money? Still less to ten million taels? I'll go back at once and give the prince your answer."
Next day, Wanyan Chi had everything in place. He received Prince Yi in the main hall. A large wooden chest sat on the floor, and his face showed his satisfaction.
"You actually raised ten million taels?"
Shen Jianchen opened the chest. "It's all here. Look it over, Your Highness. Then let her go, quickly."
Stack after stack of silver drafts lay inside, neat and thick. Wanyan Chi's eyes lit up. "You'd really hand me all this?"
Shen Jianchen said flatly, "It's not a gift. It's a trade."

"Then you love her more than I do." Wanyan Chi lifted his tea cup. "Too bad she died last night. I only wanted her to spend one night with me. She drove a dagger into her own vital spot and died on the spot. I've been grieving over it."
Shen Jianchen did not believe a word. "You're lying!"
"I love silver more than beauties. Still more ten million taels." Wanyan Chi hurled the cup down. It cracked in two with a crash.
The Jin soldiers hidden nearby heard the sound and rushed in with blades drawn.
The man meant to keep her and swindle him too. There was no avoiding a fight. Shen Jianchen threw the first punch.
Wanyan Chi's men were no match for him. Fists and feet flying, he had them all on the ground inside a quarter of an hour.
Wanyan Chi had expected this. He had other plans.
Prince Yi charged as anticipated, knocked him off his seat with one punch, seized the front of his robe and said in a voice close to an order, "Give her back!"
"I told you. She's dead."
Shen Jianchen struck him in the face and grabbed him again. "Tell me she's alive!"

Half of Wanyan Chi's face had gone black and blue. To twist the pain into distraction, he spun another lie: "I'm not like you. When it's money or a beauty, I pick money. The drafts are here. Why wouldn't I hand her over? Because I can't. If you want her, go to the potter's field outside the city. I had her body carried there last night."
He said it so smoothly that Shen Jianchen, though he still could not believe it, felt grief claw in anyway.
Wanyan Chi signaled to the guards. One of them darted in with a sharp sword.
He kept talking to hold Prince Yi's attention. "These days with her in custody, I've seen it plain. She married into the Chen family in Lin'an, but her heart stayed on one man. Want to know who?"
Shen Jianchen asked through his grief, "Who?"
Wanyan Chi said, "You."
Hearing it said aloud by someone else, tears broke loose. Shen Jianchen grabbed Wanyan Chi. "She died because of you. I'll kill you to avenge her."
Before his fist could land on a vital spot, a sword struck him from behind. Blood poured out. He dropped and lost consciousness.

Wanyan Chi straightened, smoothed his robe, and looked down at the prince with scorn. "So what if he's stronger? He lost the woman and the silver both. Men! Drag him out and dump him beyond the city."
Two guards came forward and hauled the wounded prince away.
Shen Jianchen woke in a farmer's house. Someone had dressed his wound. Cai Jing stood nearby in plain clothes. He must have been the one who saved him.
Seeing him stir, Cai Jing stepped up. "You're awake at last. No danger to your life now. Rest here until the wound closes, then get back to Bianliang as fast as you can."
Shen Jianchen asked, "Master Cai, do me one favor. Find out whether it's true… whether she's really…"
Cai Jing thought the man had lost his fortune and nearly his life over a woman. Not worth it. A small lie would finish the matter and send him on his way.

"I asked the manor guards quietly. The girl is dead, sure enough. Her body was thrown in the potter's field. I sent men to look, and they found it. I took it on myself to have her buried in waste ground outside the city."
The last of his hope went out. Shen Jianchen broke down. "Waaaah…!"
The crying held both grief and self-blame. Cai Jing nearly told the truth.
When the tears were spent, Shen Jianchen struggled up. "I'll kill Wanyan Chi and avenge her!"
His wounds were too deep. He fell back down.
Cai Jing urged him, "Wanyan Chi has doubled the guard to keep you from causing trouble. The manor is ringed with extra men and traps set every which way. Go there and you'll lose your life."
Shen Jianchen kept weeping. "She's gone. What's the point of my living?"

Cai Jing tried again, gently. "Your lordship surviving is a gift from heaven. Don't think of death. If you throw your life away, her soul won't rest easy either. Get well, visit her grave, then hurry back to Bianliang. This is no place to linger."
"Where did you bury her? Take me there now." He got up again with effort and forced himself to stay standing.
Cai Jing saw the resolve in him. The man had put his own body out of mind and would welcome death. He stopped arguing and told his servants to help Prince Yi into the carriage outside.
The new grave was Cai Jing's own arrangement, made in kindness. He did not want a good prince ruined by one woman.
They came to a bare mound of earth, the soil freshly turned. Shen Jianchen could not bear it. His legs gave way and he started to fall.
Cai Jing's two servants caught him on either side. He stayed upright, but no sound came out now. Tears ran down his face as he walked step by step toward the grave.
"Let… go of me."
The servants looked to Cai Jing. He nodded.
They let go. Shen Jianchen collapsed at the grave, body and spirit emptied out, and cried aloud. "Waaaah…!"
Cai Jing thought: Cry it out, then leave. Your life matters more.
He cried until no tears were left. His voice steadied. "Master Cai, send men to dig her up. I'll have her properly dressed and carry her back to Lin'an myself."

It was an empty grave. Cai Jing did not dare dig. He spun another tale. "Absolutely not. The dead should rest in the earth as soon as they're gone. Once buried, how can you dig them straight back up? Even if you must, wait until the forty-ninth day."
"Why?"

"After death there's an intermediate being that wanders until the forty-ninth day, when it seeks rebirth. Dig too soon and you disturb it. The body takes three or four months to turn to bone. If your lordship wants the bones for Lin'an, wait three or four months."

The word caught at Shen Jianchen. He thought of his own travel through time. What if Qianli Xun had gone back to the era they came from? If rebirth came on the forty-ninth day, he had to reach Lin'an and find the divine willow, and quickly.
He sat back on the ground. "Master Cai, find me a carriage to take me to Lin'an."
Cai Jing was glad to see him go, but the wounds were bad and the road rough. "Wouldn't it be better to wait until you're healed, Your Lordship?"
"I have to leave now." His voice was low and firm.
Cai Jing arranged it. Shen Jianchen rode alone, the carriage jolting toward Lin'an. He had medicine for the wound and the driver helped him change it. With the drug holding, the cuts began to close.
The journey took close to a month. He reached Lin'an at last. He did not call on friends or kin. He went straight to the divine willow.

Winter had come. The willow's branches were bare, with no life in them, just like his heart. He walked over the dead grass toward it, remembering how he and Qianli Xun had met in this age, and all the days that followed.
When he stood before it, his eyes were wet. "Two years and more, and she and I never came to see you. How have you been?"
The willow said nothing.
"She's dead. Do you know? You brought us here together. Can you bring her back to me just once?"
The willow said nothing.

"Why won't you speak?" he demanded. He went up to the thick trunk and threw his arms around it. "I beg you. Before the forty-ninth day is up, bring her to me. If she lives again, take my title, my wealth, my very life. Take anything."
The willow still said nothing.
"Must I die before I can find her again?"
The willow might not have heard.
"Your silence is consent. If you agree, I'll die here in front of you today. Bring her to me."
He let go of the willow, closed his fist and aimed it at his own chest. "Wait for me. I'll see you soon."
He gathered every ounce of strength into the fist and drove it toward his heart…
"Don't do it, benefactor! A suicide cannot enter the cycle of rebirth!"
The fist had not landed when Master Jingguang's voice came from behind.
At the word of no rebirth, his fist hung in the air. "You wouldn't lie to me, Master?"
"Amitabha. Those who cultivate do not speak falsehood."
"But if I don't die, how will I see her?"
"Does dying guarantee you'll see the one you long for?"
"At least I won't have to bear living alone."

"Our Buddha says a human birth is hard to come by, a precious vessel for practice. To cut it short is to make fresh karma. The old debt is not cleared, and a new one is added. Who knows how many lifetimes it will take to be free?"
"I respect the Dharma, Master, but that doesn't convince me."

"I stood nearby and heard you talking to yourself. You want to die only because the one in your heart has left you. You imagine you can kill yourself and follow her. The thought is a foolish one. Before the new karma bears its fruit and denies the dead their rest—"
Shen Jianchen lowered his fist and turned. His wet eyes were full of question. "Why would she lose her rest?"

Seeing he was listening, Master Jingguang spoke patiently. "If she had not died, you would not be dying. She is the cause, you the effect. The two are bound together in the cycle. Slight the body as you plan to, and the karma you make will come back on her. You keep saying it's for her. The truth is you can't bear your own pain. You're being selfish, thinking only of your own relief, never seeing what you bring on her in the next world."
The words struck like a morning bell and a evening drum. Shen Jianchen woke.
He thought of how he had clung to his claim on Qianli Xun and gone to seize a bride, making trouble for her and for himself, until she spent nearly two years in prison. The master had a point.
He bowed. "Your words wake the deaf, Master. I was asleep and now I see. From this day I'll live well, not for myself but for her."
Master Jingguang smiled. "You are a blessed man to understand my poor words. Because your roots run deep, I'll add a little more."
"Please, Master."
"You cannot put her from your mind. Do good in her name. It will steady the living and gather merit for the dead. She will benefit in the next world."

Shen Jianchen's eyes grew wet again. At last he had found a way to live out his days without her. He would do good under Qianli Xun's name, and let others praise her, so that she would seem still at his side.
"Thank you, Master."
"Amitabha." Master Jingguang wore a kind smile and walked away.
Master Jingguang's words had turned him from suicide. Shen Jianchen came to the Chen gate heavy with grief.

A servant announced that Prince Yi was outside asking for him. Chen Haoyu came out in a hurry, anger and dread on his face. He took no notice of the hollow, lost look on the prince and landed a punch. "Bai Feng told me my wife was seized by the Jin in Yanjing. It's your fault! Who told you to take her there?"
Shen Jianchen did not raise a hand. He let the punches land. Another one struck him.
Chen Haoyu grabbed his collar. "Bai Feng says you went to save her. Where is she? Why did only you come back?"
"She… is dead."
Chen Haoyu shoved him hard. "You're lying!"
"She's buried outside Yanjing. I saw it with my own eyes…"
"Liar! You won't give her back, so you made this up!"
"I'm not lying. No one wants her alive more than I do."

Chen Haoyu saw the red rims around the prince's eyes, the weight dragging him down, the handsome face aged in a moment. He had to believe. His raised fist could not come down. He squatted on the ground and wept. "Waaaah…!"

After a while he stood and started back toward the house, saying as he went, "I'll make ready and go to Yanjing myself. I'll bring my wife's bones home to Lin'an and bury them in the Chen family plot…"
"She's not a Chen any more. You have no right to her bones."
Chen Haoyu stopped and spun around. He closed the distance and seized the prince's collar again. "The imperial edict forced me to end the marriage. In my heart she is my wife, always."
"However you feel, she's mine now."
"What does that mean? Did you tell her about the edict?"

Shen Jianchen wanted her to belong to him alone, even dead. "Yes, I told her. She was relieved. She said the marriage had forced her to follow you against her wishes again and again. With it gone, she could finally be with the man she loved. She came to Yanjing with me willingly. She didn't come back to Lin'an for you."

"You lie! Listen. The Jin army is coming south. Bianliang will be attacked soon. No one knows what will happen to the man on the throne. When the time comes the edict will be void, and she'll be my wife again!"
"Whatever the His Majesty does, it's too late. Because… because in Yanjing, we consummated our marriage…"
Before he finished, Chen Haoyu's fist struck his face. On the careworn face, another bruise bloomed.
"Liar! You're lying!" Chen Haoyu's voice tore at the edges.

"I've said what I had to say. You're luckier than I. At least she was yours for a time while she lived. My hours alone with her were too few. And still you aren't satisfied? Still you'd fight me for her after she's gone? Don't I deserve some pity?" Tears rolled from the corners of his eyes.
Something in it touched Chen Haoyu. He did not want to argue further. He turned and walked into the Chen house, limp as a plant struck by frost.
At the door he stopped, his back to Prince Yi. "I won't fight you. What good would it do? She won't come back to life."

Shen Jianchen watched the slumped figure disappear before he thought to leave. Where now? His life had lost its direction. Wherever Qianli Xun was, there had been a life for him. Now she was gone, the direction was gone, and he did not know which road to take.
The manor in Bianliang was sold. He would not go back. Soon the Jin would take the city. Youlin Retreat, where he had lived, was never his home either.
Only the bamboo house counted as home. From the moment he thought of building it, it had been built for him and Qianli Xun.
He walked out of the city on foot. Without the woman he loved, why race against time? Time had to be worn down slowly, and the wearing of it might dull the hollow ache inside.
Just past the gate, a carriage pulled up. Qiao Wenxian stepped down.
"I heard you were back and was on my way to find you."
"How did you know?"
"Someone from Youlin Retreat saw you in the street and said you were heading toward the Chen house. I was going there to look for you. Lucky I didn't waste the trip. We met on the road."
With Wenyuan, Shen Jianchen did not want to hold himself together. He let go, went up and threw his arms around him, and cried. "Waaaah! Wenyuan, she's gone. I'll never see her again, waaaah…!"

Wenyuan held him and said, "Seeing you like this, I guessed as much. If I'd ignored my family and taken her away back then, none of this would have happened. Don't grieve so. Come back to Youlin Retreat with me."

Ever since Prince Yi and his consort returned to Bianliang, Qiao Wenxian had lived at Youlin Retreat with his wife and concubine. Before long Miao Zhiyu bore a son and Xiaguo a daughter. Both children were past two and already running all over the floor.
The Qiao elders were well pleased with a son and a daughter, and doubly glad they had not chosen the Zhu girl all those years ago. Otherwise the Qiaos would be the ones twisting inside now.
Qiao Wenxian did not see it that way. His mind was on Shuzhen. He hoped all went well with her.
At Youlin Retreat he bathed, changed into clothes Wenyuan had set out, ate a simple meal, and came back to himself a little. But the look in Shen Jianchen's eyes still said one thing: lost.
Qiao Wenxian had not brought Miao Zhiyu, Xiaguo or the children to greet Prince Yi. He was in too low a state, and seeing his own son and daughter would only hurt him more. Another few days, then.
The two sat facing each other at a table indoors, a brazier burning bright beside them. The room was warm.
The cold he had carried all the way from Yanjing was gone now. The cold in his body had lifted. The cold in his heart had not.

Qiao Wenxian filled his cup of sweet wine, then his own. "Bai Feng told me when he brought Matron Zou back. You sold the manor in Bianliang and everything you owned to raise the silver. Ah. I'm ashamed to be less than you."
"Without her, what is money for?" Shen Jianchen lifted his cup and drained it. "Now she's gone, it means even less."
"We haven't seen each other in two years and more. Much has changed. The court is plainly finished. I'm afraid the whole realm will fall to the Jin."
"The Jin have no claim on the realm. At most they'll split it with Song, and in the end they'll be destroyed too. Pity we won't live to see that day."
"How do you know?"
A rare smile crossed his face. "I guessed."
Qiao Wenxian raised his glass. "Right or wrong, it's what I wanted to hear. If we won't live to see that day, then drink with me now and toast it early."
Shen Jianchen poured for himself and touched cups with Wenyuan.
Qiao Wenxian set down his cup. "What will you do now?"
Shen Jianchen was silent a moment. "I'll go back to the bamboo house that was hers and mine, and end my days there."
Then, remembering Master Jingguang, he added, "I'll do good works in her name. When people speak of her, it will be as if she were still at my side."
Qiao Wenxian was moved. "Count me in?"
"You already took her first love. Now you want a share of this too?"
"It wasn't I who took her first love. It was Master Xu."
"Looks the same to me."
"Fine. I won't compete with you."
"This is better. No one to fight me, and Mengrong won't be there to stop me. I can be with her without a care. Except she…" His voice broke and tears came again.
"I heard from Bai Feng about the princess consort and Xilan too. I'm sorry."
Shen Jianchen lifted his head and held back another wave of tears. "When spring comes next year I'll go back to Yanjing and bring all their bones home to Lin'an."

Qiao Wenxian did not want him drowning in grief and steered toward Lin'an talk. "Ever since the eunuch Liang turned Lin'an inside out, the Eastern Poetry Society has hardly met. The new prefect banned it. Eastern Chenze keeps small gatherings in private, as in the old days. Then he and An Mingxuan married, and with families to raise there were even fewer. Add the unrest, and no one's in the mood for refined pursuits. The poetry scene in Lin'an is nothing like it was."
"Without her, the gatherings lost half their shine. What's the point?"

The turn failed. Qiao Wenxian tried another. "There is one piece of good news. At Mid-Autumn this year Cao Ban brought Ye Anya back to Lin'an. Their son is past two, and for the grandson's sake the Cao family accepted her. A few old friends can gather again. That's a rare joy. I'll call everyone together one of these days to keep you company."
"If they'd brought her out of prison on Mid-Autumn and sent her straight back to Lin'an, none of this would have happened. It's my fault for clinging to the days alone with her."

That failed too. He pressed on. "You know? Madam Jiang had a hard delivery last year. Jiang wanted to save the mother, but she refused. She insisted on saving the child. They got a son, and she let go. Sad when you think of it."
Remembering Tianmu Mountain, Shen Jianchen found no pity in him. "The Buddhists say good and evil each get their due. Seems true enough."

Qiao Wenxian had just begun to smile at the change of subject when he heard Prince Yi say, "She was so kind, always thinking of others and putting herself out, and this is how it ends? Where's the justice in good and evil getting their due?"

The third attempt collapsed. He dropped the smile and grabbed at another topic. "It does happen, you know. Lin Jue's concubine Chun Jinqiao took a strange sickness last year. No doctor could touch it. She died this summer. People said it privately: born a songgirl, low to begin with, she traded her looks for the great ladies of Lin'an to come and worship at her door. She had no luck to carry it, and it killed her."
Shen Jianchen rebuked him. "Since when do Lin'an's talents turn into gossips, chattering about other people's household affairs?"
"I don't want to gossip. You've been away so long. I'm telling you what's changed in two years."
"How is Lin Jue now?"
The turn finally worked. Qiao Wenxian teased him. "Look who's talking. You're prying into other people's households yourself."
"Say no more and I'll go." Shen Jianchen made to stand.

Qiao Wenxian stopped him. "Don't rush off. Two years and more—we need to talk. You're not leaving tonight. Stay at Youlin Retreat. Tomorrow I'll take you out to the bamboo house in the country myself."

With Prince Yi settled again, Qiao Wenxian went on. "Lin Jue knows how to climb better than anyone. The post of Commander of All Armies sits easy on him. His nature isn't bad, and he knows where to draw the line. Chun Jinqiao's death shook him badly. No more concubines, no more houses of pleasure. He settles down with Bai Meruo. She's given him a daughter, the same age as my two."
"I envy you. You're both parents now. And she and I…"
He had dragged it back again. Every attempt had failed, but Qiao Wenxian kept hunting for something new.
Before he could find one, Nanshuang came in. "Your Lordship, Master Qiao. Commander Lin is here to pay his respects."
Qiao Wenxian said, "He must have heard you were back. Shall I receive him?"
Shen Jianchen said, "Why not? We're old friends. And back then he did me some good turns."
Qiao Wenxian told Nanshuang, "Show Commander Lin in."

Nanshuang went out. Lin Jue lifted the heavy curtain and came in. The cold outside had reddened his cheeks and nose. The heat of the room hit him all at once, and the clash of hot and cold left him glowing.
He bowed. "My respects to His Lordship Prince Yi."
Shen Jianchen said evenly, "No Prince Yi today. Just friends. Sit and have a drink."
Lin Jue did not dare. He dropped to his knees. "I've come to confess before your lordship with my own mouth. I'd give my life for it if you asked."
"Confess what?"
"If I hadn't taken her from the Chen house that day, none of what followed would have happened. It's my fault. Do with me what you will—kill me, flay me."

Shen Jianchen laughed twice, coldly. "Hmph. If she hadn't been willing, could you have walked her out so easily? My life is worth nothing to me. If you're so free with yours, go to Bianliang and help your His Majesty fight the Jin. Dying on a battlefield is worth more than dying by my hand."
"Even without your lordship saying it, I intended to. I've asked the prefect to let me lead troops to Bianliang tomorrow as reinforcements."
"Then why come here playing at remorse and asking me to take your life?"
"Only to show I'm sorry."
"She never blamed you. Get up. Sit and talk."
"Thank you for sparing me." Lin Jue stood, pulled over a chair and sat at the table.
Qiao Wenxian set a cup before him and filled it.
The three drank and talked over old times until dark. When Prince Yi wanted to rest, Lin Jue finally left.
Qiao Wenxian told Nanshuang to see to Prince Yi and went back to his own room.
He had barely crossed the threshold when wife and concubine blocked his way.
Miao Zhiyu asked, "Prince Yi is back. Where's Youqi Jushi?"
Xiaguo asked, "Nanshuang says the young mistress is gone. Is it true?"
Qiao Wenxian groaned. "I'd just calmed him down, and here you come."
"Then it's true." Xiaguo wept. "Waaaah. The mistress was good. Why do the good never last?"
Miao Zhiyu took it better. She helped Xiaguo to a chair and sat her down. "Don't grieve, sister. Wenyuan hasn't given us an answer yet."
Hope kindled again. "Well? What is it?"
Qiao Wenxian sighed. "Prince Yi says Shuzhen and the princess consort are buried outside Bianliang. In spring he'll take their bones back to Lin'an."
With the answer confirmed, Xiaguo cried all the harder. "Mistress, how could you leave us? Waaaah…!"
Miao Zhiyu shed a few tears too. "Without Youqi Jushi, the poetry circle in Lin'an is finished."
Wenyuan made a vow. "From this day I'll attend no poetry gathering and no gathering of literati at all, unless Shuzhen rises from the dead."
At that, both women cried out loud, grieving for the one who was gone, and grieving for the place she held in Wenyuan's heart.
Once Wanyan Chi had the men drag Shen Jianchen out of the city, he went down to the underground chamber and said, "Time's up. The Prince Yi of Song hasn't come. Stop dreaming that he'll pay for you."

Ten million taels was no small sum. To raise it, the prince would have to smash pots and sell iron until nothing was left. Qianli Xun did not want that. She could never repay him in this life or the next.
"I've never dreamed of it. All I think is when you'll die under my fists."
"You may be stronger than me, but you can't do anything to me."
Wanyan Chi came closer. Qianli Xun saw the bruise on his face and sneered. "Beaten like that and you still have the nerve to show off in front of me?" She shot out a punch.
They traded a few blows. He knew he could not win and backed off, stamped twice on the floor, and a net dropped from above and caught her.

During her captivity he had snared her with that mechanism more than once. She had studied it closely in the chamber and tried the same movement herself. It never worked. Caught again, she snapped, "Only a man with no real skill uses tricks like that on me!"
Wanyan Chi approached the woman in the net. "If you behaved, I wouldn't need tricks."
"Pah!"
He was not angry. "When my master comes from Huining with the witch doctor's medicine, I'll make you drink it. You'll turn soft and sweet."
Qianli Xun had never feared anything in her life. Now fear crept in.
"Don't be afraid. I won't hurt you. I mean to pull the thorns out of you so I can get close and make you mine."
"You bastard."
"Curse me all you like. It won't make me angry. Once you're mine, I'll take you out of this hole and show you the grand rivers and mountains of my Great Jin."

At the words "grand rivers and mountains," she thought the Jin must already be marching on Bianliang. She said deliberately, "The Jin army is attacking Song. Why are you hiding in Yanjing enjoy yourself like a turtle in a shell? No man would do that!"

He did not take the bait. "Trying to rouse me? Hah. Useless. Our two armies will take Bianliang with ease. I'm not needed. Someone has to hold Yanjing, you know. Guarding a city can be harder than taking one. I know you want me gone so you can bolt. I won't fall for it. Better spend your time thinking how to please me, so your life here will be easier."
The taunt had failed. Try feeling instead. "Wanyan Chi, I saved your life. A life saved deserves a spring reported a thousandfold. You don't treat your rescuer like this."
"Exactly because you saved my life, I want to give myself to you and make you my woman."
They had come full circle. Qianli Xun reminded him, "A melon forced off the vine isn't sweet."

He had his own logic. "A forced melon suits me fine. Crisp and fresh, hard to come by. That's the one a man dreams about and clings to. Let it ripen and drop into my hand on its own—sweet, yes, but soft and slack. Two bites and I'd push it aside."

This was the most shameless, most stubborn man she had ever met. No argument touched him. "I'm not easy to handle. You'd best give up. If pushed, I'll die right in front of you, and you'll get nothing for your trouble."
"I won't let you die before I have you. Live. Wait for the pleasure I'll bring you."
He walked out, stamped lightly outside the door, and the net around her rose back to the ceiling.
Qianli Xun stood, went to the spot where he had stamped and stamped herself several times. Nothing. She went to the door and stamped again. Still nothing.
"The mechanism in this place is strange. Why doesn't stamping work for me? Does it answer only to Wanyan Chi?"
A maid came over to coax her. "Don't cross the young prince again, miss. This chamber is full of traps. You'll only get the worst of it."
She seized the chance. "Were all the traps in this place installed by Wanyan Chi?"
"Probably not. The young prince only moved into the manor not long ago. The previous owner may have set them."
Qianli Xun frowned. "Then why do the traps answer only to Wanyan Chi's footsteps?"
The maid shook her head. "This slave doesn't know."
The workmanship was too clever for an outsider like her to follow. She gave up studying it, went into the room, lay on the couch and thought her own thoughts.
The maid stood quietly to one side.

Qianli Xun did not know Mengrong was dead. She still wished Prince Yi and Mengrong well. By her count they should be back in Bianliang. She hoped Mengrong had recovered after taking Liu Miaoshou's medicine.

She thought of Chen Haoyu. She had been away so long; he must be frantic. If he learned the Jin had taken her, would he run to Yanjing? She hoped not. Let him mind the Chen business. If she never got back to Lin'an, she hoped he would marry someone else.

Worst of all were the elders at home. Jail, then stranded in Yanjing—they must be sick with worry. She hoped they looked after their health, and if she did not return safe, that they would not grieve too much.
Looking back, her whole road could be summed up in one word: rough. Put it bluntly, her luck had always been bad.

Before the crossing she wrote novels and got torn apart online. After the crossing she lived in another woman's skin, and the luck stayed bad. She thought again of Master Jingguang's words, of right thought and right intention. She had held to what she believed was right all the way here, and thought her karma was spent, that a quiet life lay ahead. Instead she had fallen into Wanyan Chi's hands.
What could she do now, let alone keep right thought and right intention? She let out a sigh. "Ah."
The maid beside her heard it and offered, "You're so fortunate, miss. Why sigh?"
Qianli Xun sat up and threw her a look. "Which eye of yours sees me as fortunate?"
"I've never seen the young prince care for a woman like this. Don't you feel lucky, miss?"
"I'd rather do without that kind of luck!"
"You don't know, miss. Back in Huining, girls of good families wanted to be his side consort and he looked at none of them. But he's gone to such trouble for you. Even we servants are moved."
"Hmph." She sneered, then changed course. She might learn something useful from the girl. "Hey. If you're so moved, tell me about Wanyan Chi. Maybe once I know more I'll take a liking to him."
"What would you like to know, miss? Ask anything."
"How many women has he got?"
"One wife and three side consorts in the prince's manor."
With all those women, why is he still chasing?
"What does 'chasing' mean?"
"It means a man who has a wife still runs after other women."
The maid thought it over. "You're wrong about the young prince, miss."
Qianli Xun's eyes went wide. "Wrong? The facts are right in front of me. How am I wrong?"
"The wife and three side consorts were arranged by his elders. He didn't want any of them, but he had to marry them. Ah. He looks splendid on the outside, but he's had a hard life."
"Him, pitiful? If he's pitiful, is the whole world a pack of pitiful wretches?"

"You don't know, miss. His mother died when he was small. When he grew up he finally met a woman he loved, but His Majesty forced him to marry a minister's daughter, to bind the ministers close, they say. He refused, again and again, and His Majesty…"

The maid leaned close and whispered, "had the woman he loved killed. He called him a bastard born of a Han. To stand firm in Great Jin, he had to marry a minister's daughter. That's how he ended up with one wife and three side consorts."
Qianli Xun said without warmth, "Serves him right."
The maid straightened. "And look closely, miss. You're a bit like the woman he loved. No wonder he treats you differently."
"You've seen her?"
"Not in person. Only a portrait. The eyes and brows are somewhat like yours."
"So what if we're alike? We're not the same person." Then she asked, "Why was Wanyan Chi born of a Han woman?"

The maid put a finger to her lips and hushed her, glanced all around, then came back and lowered her voice. "They say when His Majesty was still a prince, he traveled in the south, met a Han woman and fell in love. The young prince was born of her. Not long after, someone carried the baby to Huining and dropped him into the arms of a guard at the prince's manor. As he grew, the young prince went south many times looking for his birth mother. Every trip ended in disappointment."
At last Qianli Xun understood why she had met him in Lin'an. Could his mother be from Lin'an?

The maid lowered her voice again and pressed the point. "He's even said that if he could see his mother just once in this life, he'd give his life for it. A man with such feeling and such duty—what reason have you to refuse him, miss?"
She had listened a long while, found no way to handle him, and instead felt sorry for him. Qianli Xun eyed the maid sideways. "You're a clever maid. Your young prince ought to reward you properly."
The maid said quickly, "Don't tell him, miss. A slave who talks about her master's private affairs behind his back gets beaten."
"Hmph. When all's said, he's no good."
"The young prince is good!"
"A good man beats his maid over a little thing like this?"
"There's a saying: a state has its laws, a house has its rules."
"You're quick to excuse him. However you see it, I see no good in him."
Sullen at Wanyan Chi, Qianli Xun stayed in the underground chamber five more days. The good part was that he did not come near. The bad part was that she still could not get out.
The longer she sat alone with nothing to do, the more Prince Yi's face rose in her mind. A quiet thought now and then did no harm. In a boredom like this, memory was all she had to pass the time.
She smiled, remembering their hunt for the miracle doctor through Yanjing's streets. The smile had barely come when she heard the chamber door open. It vanished at once.
Before long Wanyan Chi walked in, a maid behind him carrying a pot of wine and two cups.
Qianli Xun demanded, "What do you want?"
"To see you. And to bring you good news."
He sat at the table. The maid set out the pot and cups and slipped out.
She watched him warily. "What good news?"
"Today I'll take you out of this place. It's dark underground, no sun. Stay too long and it will damage your health."
"You'd be that kind?"
"When will you truly understand how good I am to you?" His smile was half there, half teasing.
Disgust crossed her face. "Save it. If you mean to take me out, let's go now."
"No hurry. Drink a couple of cups with me first."
"Sorry. I never drink."
"It's only osmanthus brew made by Han hands. Not real wine."
She stared at the pot. Five days ago he had mentioned the witch doctor's medicine. She was more on guard than ever. "You haven't put something in that brew to make me drink it and do what you want?"

"The witch doctor's medicine? I made that up to frighten you. Foolish of you to take it seriously." Seeing she would not bite, he let a trace of sorrow show and used the reason he had prepared. "The truth is, today is my mother's birthday. I never knew her, and I never knew the day she was born, so I took my own birth date for hers. Every year on this day I drink alone, thinking of a mother I never saw."
She was touched a little, but still wary. "Hmph. Who knows if it's true?"

"Why would I lie about my mother? She is the greatest pain of my life. Let me tell you this. She was from Lin'an, like you. She was the younger sister of Shao Zhengye of the Shao escrow house. I went to Lin'an to find her. Shao Zhengye told me she was dead and told me not to trouble the Shao family again. I asked where she was buried. They would not say. So I slipped into the Shao burial grounds. No stone bore her name. I searched every graveyard in Lin'an. Nothing. I have a strong feeling she's still alive. She simply doesn't want to see me…"
His eyes had gone red when he spoke of his mother. She could see the feeling was real, and her guard dropped a little. "You're Jin. It's only natural she wouldn't want to see you."
"Once Great Jin takes Bianliang and the matter is settled, I'll go back to Lin'an and turn the Shao house upside down. I won't rest until I find her."
"I'd let it go. If she doesn't want to see you, why disturb her?"
"You can't know what it's like for a child who's had no mother since the day he was born."
She thought of herself before the crossing, motherless from childhood too, though luckier than him: she had at least known a mother's love. "Of course I know."
"If you know, then sit with me and drink two cups. Call it pity for a motherless child."
Under the weight of that feeling, every defence fell. "All right. Two cups with you. Say it plainly—two cups, then you let me out."
"Agreed. Two cups, then I take you out." He put on a look of honest feeling.
She sat down at the table with no suspicion left. He filled both cups and lifted his. "Together, then."
She raised hers carefully. "This one's for your mother. I hope you find her soon."
He could not wait. He touched cups and drank it down.
She watched him swallow without a pause, decided the brew was clean, and drank. It tasted good. Better than any osmanthus brew she had ever had.

She poured another and lifted it. "A man who's thought of his mother since he was small can't be bad. If you're not bad, then let me go early. I'm from Lin'an; I know that place better than you. Let me go back and leave finding your mother to me. I'll see it done, guaranteed…"
She had not finished when her head swam. The cup dropped onto the table and the brew spilled across it.
Her eyes barely open, Wanyan Chi was beside her in a flash. She fell into his arms.
Her eyes were clouded. "You… lied." Then she passed out.
A satisfied smile spread over his face. "Unless I lie, how will you ever behave?"
